call.result: May 2, 2019 · Abstract: Recently an unidentified emission line at 3.55 keV has been detected in X-ray spectra of clusters of galaxies. The line has been discussed as a possible decay signature of 7.1 keV sterile neutrinos, which have been proposed as a dark matter (DM) candidate. Jan 4, 2019 · We use a combined 1.2 Ms of NuSTAR observations of M31 to search for X-ray lines from sterile neutrino dark matter decay. For the first time in a NuSTAR analysis, we consistently take into account the signal contribution from both the focused and unfocused fields of view. An unidentified emission line at 3.55keV was recently detected in X-ray spectra of clusters of galaxies. The line has been discussed as a possible decay signature of 7.1keV sterile neutrinos, which have been proposed as a dark matter (DM) candidate. We aim to put constraints on the proposed line emission in a large sample of Chandra-observed clusters and obtain limits on the mixing angle in a 7.1 keV sterile neutrino DM scenario. brief.summary: Literature shows sterile neutrino DM in the keV range is constrained jointly by BBN (Delta N_eff, Yp, D/H) and X-ray decay searches (E=m_s/2 line). BBN constraints arise from thermalization via active-sterile oscillations increasing N_eff and altering n/p freeze-out, with relaxation possible via large lepton asymmetry or secret interactions. X-ray constraints come from non-observation of decay lines in stacked clusters, M31, Galactic Center/Bulge and diffuse background with NuSTAR, Chandra, XMM-Newton, with the 3.55 keV / 7.1 keV candidate extensively tested and largely excluded as DM decay. Production mechanism (Dodelson-Widrow non-resonant vs Shi-Fuller resonant vs inflaton decay) determines relic density vs mixing relation and maps to joint exclusion plane with Lyman-alpha free-streaming limits.

delta:
**Survey** — 32 tools on 3 servers, 6 read-only probes, 6 papers found.

Literature shows sterile neutrino DM in the keV range is constrained jointly by BBN (Delta N_eff, Yp, D/H) and X-ray decay searches (E=m_s/2 line). BBN constraints arise from thermalization via active-sterile oscillations increasing N_eff and altering n/p freeze-out, with relaxation possible via large lepton asymmetry or secret interactions. X-ray constraints come from non-observation of decay lines in stacked clusters, M31, Galactic Center/Bulge and diffuse background with NuSTAR, Chandra, XMM-Newton, with the 3.55 keV / 7.1 keV candidate extensively tested and largely excluded as DM decay. Production mechanism (Dodelson-Widrow non-resonant vs Shi-Fuller resonant vs inflaton decay) determines relic density vs mixing relation and maps to joint exclusion plane with Lyman-alpha free-streaming limits.

Quantities worth checking: Delta N_eff from sterile thermalization vs (m_s, sin^2 2theta); Primordial Yp (He-4 mass fraction) shift vs Delta N_eff; Primordial D/H shift vs Delta N_eff and baryon-to-photon ratio; Sterile decay rate Gamma ~ 1.38e-29 s^-1 (m_s/1keV)^5 sin^2 2theta and lifetime tau; X-ray photon energy E_gamma = m_s/2 and line flux vs J-factor/distance; Relic density Omega_s h^2 for Dodelson-Widrow / Shi-Fuller / inflaton-decay production.

directions.goal: Deepen the weakest X-ray decay-line claim (f-017/x-02): rebuild the 7.1/10/20/40/50 keV sin^2 2theta limit table from primary sources and rerun the X-ray/BBN emulator at a contrasting high-mass SPI-dominated point.
directions.rationale: Prior table (f-017) has only the XRISM 7.1 keV limit read from a primary source; 10/20/40 keV NuSTAR entries rely on a secondary summary of arXiv:2405.17861 Fig.3 which was never numerically read, and the 50 keV SPI entry has a 7-dex lifetime vs mixing mismatch (tool tau 7.8e26 s at 3e-14 vs quoted 1e20 s). Tool support is thin: only 7.1 keV/1e-10 and 20 keV/1e-12 were run through predict_sterile_nu_xray_line, with no contrasting 40-50 keV low-mixing point where INTEGRAL/SPI dominates and BBN Delta N_eff is negligible.
steps: Call describe_sterile_nu_tools to confirm current baselines (Yp, D/H, N_eff, validity N_eff 2.044-6.044, m_s<100 keV, Delta chi2>3.84) and X-ray J-factor assumptions.

Rerun predict_sterile_nu_xray_line at contrasting points vs prior 7.1 keV/1e-10: (a) m_s=40 keV, sin^2 2theta=3e-14 (SPI regime, E=20 keV) and (b) m_s=10 keV, sin^2 2theta=1e-12 (NuSTAR regime, E=5 keV); record Gamma=1.38e-29*(m_s/1keV)^5*sin^2 2theta, tau, E_gamma=m_s/2, and built-in NuSTAR/XMM exclusion flag.

delta:
**Plan** — 3 lines of investigation:
1. Deepen the weakest X-ray decay-line claim (f-017/x-02): rebuild the 7.1/10/20/40/50 keV sin^2 2theta limit table from primary sources and rerun the X-ray/BBN emulator at a contrasting high-mass SPI-dominated point. — Prior table (f-017) has only the XRISM 7.1 keV limit read from a primary source; 10/20/40 keV NuSTAR entries rely on a secondary summary of arXiv:2405.17861 Fig.3 which was never numerically read, and the 50 keV SPI entry has a 7-dex lifetime vs mixing mismatch (tool tau 7.8e26 s at 3e-14 vs quoted 1e20 s). Tool support is thin: only 7.1 keV/1e-10 and 20 keV/1e-12 were run through predict_sterile_nu_xray_line, with no contrasting 40-50 keV low-mixing point where INTEGRAL/SPI dominates and BBN Delta N_eff is negligible.
2. Deepen the weakest production-mechanism / structure-formation claim (f-018/f-021/d-09 blocked): settle the DW normalization factor 10-17x dispute, quote the Viel+2005 m_th->m_s coefficient verbatim, and test SF vs DW at a contrasting low-mixing point. — Viability table (f-018) rests on abstracts only for 3/4 2024-2026 papers (2502.17374, 2609.31340, 2601.03346); the DW Omega_s h^2=0.12 line differs by 10-17x between server (2.55e-10 at 7.1 keV) and Abazajian arXiv:1705.01837 Eq.37 (3.0e-9 at 7.1 keV) without verbatim Eq.37 quote; the Viel+2005 m_s=4.43 keV*(m_th/1keV)^{4/3} coefficient was used but never quoted; SF L>~0.5 viable region (2507.18752: m_s>~10 keV, sin^2 2theta<~1e-14) cannot be tested by server (L cap 0.1, heuristic Delta N_eff=0.1xDW, no xi_e). No contrasting SF vs DW grid at same mass/mixing exists.
3. Synthesize all prior and new results into an updated joint BBN+X-ray report with provenance and robustness checks. — Board has 10 directions with fragmented findings (f-001 to f-022, x-01/x-02) and two blocked/open items (d-09 bibliography, d-06 Viel quote); the final deliverable requires a single reproducible report that integrates the two deepened claims above, corrects the factor-3/10x normalization and SPI mismatch, and provides explicit BBN (Delta N_eff, Yp, D/H) and X-ray (Gamma, tau, E_gamma, flux) numbers per mechanism.
Critic's view: revise — SPI lifetime mismatch (tool tau 7.8e26 s vs quoted 1e20 s at 50 keV/3e-14) cannot be resolved without primary SPI paper. web_search step is vague ('e.g. Boyarsky/Roach') - must target specific arXiv ID (e.g. 2008.02283, 2207.04572, or 2405.17861 SPI comparison) and cite verbatim definition of sin^2 2theta normalization, f_DM=1 assumption, and profile/J-factor used for conversion.; get_paper_figures returns images+captions only, not numeric tables. Claiming 'numerically read Fig.3 values at 7,10,20,40 keV' will be manual digitization - must be labeled as approximate with estimated uncertainty and figure number, not as exact tool output, to remain verifiable.; DW normalization 10-17x dispute requires verbatim Abazajian arXiv:1705.01837 Eq.37 quote with URL via cite(). Plan includes this but success depends on capturing full equation including 0.527*erfc term and noting T_QCD 150-200 MeV uncertainty; without quote the corrected table is unverifiable..

**Wave 1** — now exploring, in parallel: Deepen the weakest X-ray decay-line claim (f-017/x-02): rebuild the 7.1/10/20/40/50 keV sin^2 2theta limit table from primary sources and rerun the X-ray/BBN emulator at a contrasting high-mass SPI-dominated point.; Deepen the weakest production-mechanism / structure-formation claim (f-018/f-021/d-09 blocked): settle the DW normalization factor 10-17x dispute, quote the Viel+2005 m_th->m_s coefficient verbatim, and test SF vs DW at a contrasting low-mixing point.; Synthesize all prior and new results into an updated joint BBN+X-ray report with provenance and robustness checks..

Abstract: Sterile neutrinos offer a minimal and testable explanation for dark matter (DM), with their radiative decay actively searched for in X-ray observations. We show that cold sterile neutrino DM can be efficiently produced during reheating from inflaton decays with a small branching ratio, BR ≲ 10−4. args.claim: DW vs SF at m_s=20 keV, sin^2 2theta=1e-14: DW gives Delta N_eff=1.42e-07, Omega_s h^2=3.04e-05, Delta chi2_BBN=-0.0 (BBN-allowed, not overclosing); SF (L=0.1 max, heuristic 0.1xDW) gives Delta N_eff=1.42e-08, Omega_s h^2=4.90, Delta chi2_BBN=-0.0 (BBN-allowed but overcloses by 40x); at 50 keV, 1e-14: DW Omega_s h^2=1.58e-04, SF Omega_s h^2=30.6, both BBN-allowed, SF overcloses by 255x, demonstrating server SF heuristic is unphysical at L=0.1 and cannot test L>0.5 viable region.

Dec 20, 2005 · Sterile neutrinos with masses in the keV range are viable candidates for the warm dark matter. We analyze existing data for the extragalactic diffuse X-ray background for signatures of sterile neutrino decay. Sterile neutrinos with masses in the keV range are viable candidates for the warm dark matter. We analyze existing data for the extragalactic diffuse X-ray background for signatures of sterile neutrino decay. Similarly, the signal from radiative sterile neutrino decays accumulated over the history of the Universe could be seen as a feature in the diffuse extragalactic background light spectrum. call.result: Using a quasiclassical Boltzmann transport calculation of the dark matter production, we compute the nonthermal phase space distributions of sterile neutrinos across a broad range of particle mass $ {m}_ {s}$ and mixing angle $ {\mathrm {sin}}^ {2} (2\ensuremath {\theta})$ parameter space. In this paper, we examine the Shi-Fuller sterile neutrino dark matter production mechanism given the newly uncovered possibility of large lepton numbers in the early Universe, during the dark matter production era. The ordinary and dark matter in the Universe may share a common origin in the framework of a minimal extension of the Standard Model by three right-handed neutrinos. A pair of such heavy neutral leptons (HNLs) can give masses to neutrinos, generate the baryon asymmetry at the electroweak scale and produce a large lepton asymmetry at the QCD scale, which is then resonantly transformed into an ... Finally, we note that the lepton potential in sterile neutrino dark matter production depends on the total lepton number in an asymmetric way, with a factor of 2 greater dependence on the lepton number in the species with which the sterile neutrino mixes. Here, we propose a new solution where scalar-mediated nonstandard interactions between active and sterile neutrinos (𝜈 𝑎 − 𝜈 𝑠) lead to new production channels for sterile neutrino DM, independent of the active-sterile mixing and without the need for any fine-tuned resonance or primordial lepton asymmetries.

call.result: One of the most promising WDM candidates is a sterile (right-handed) neutrino with a mass in the keV range, which could explain the pulsar velocity kick [4], help in reionizing the Universe at high redshift [5], and emerging from many particle physics models with grand unification (e.g., [6,7]). Aug 1, 2006 · This plot summarizes some of the parameter space constraints (at the 95% C.L.) for the sterile neutrino models, assuming that they constitute the dark matter. Limits are explained in the text. Jan 26, 2005 · We present new transfer function fits for thermal WDM candidates in particle mass regimes beyond the range of previous work, and at the scales of current and upcoming constraints. Jan 4, 2012 · Abstract A sterile neutrino with a mass around the keV scale could be an interesting candidate for warm dark matter. For a certain class of composite neutrino theories, these sterile neutrinos naturally have the appropriate mixing angles to be resonantly produced warm dark matter (WDM).

report:
# Sterile neutrino DM: BBN + X-ray joint constraints — updated report

## Abstract
This run attempted to deepen the two weakest claims from prior work: the X-ray decay-line limit table and the production-mechanism / structure-formation mapping. Two contrasting X-ray emulator points and a six-point BBN grid at 40–50 keV were computed locally, and literature figures were extracted for NuSTAR stray-light limits, Abazajian review detections, and Viel et al. WDM transfer functions. Tool budget was exhausted after four calls per direction, so no primary-source verbatim quotes, no numerically read NuSTAR Fig.3 or XRISM limits, no SPI primary fetch, no DW-normalization settlement, and no BBN robustness reruns were completed. The joint BBN+X-ray exclusion therefore remains anchored to prior-run scans and server heuristics with explicit caveats.

## Background
Literature describes keV sterile neutrino dark matter constrained jointly by BBN and X-ray decay searches. BBN constraints arise from thermalization via active-sterile oscillations increasing N_eff and altering n/p freeze-out, with relaxation possible via large lepton asymmetry or secret interactions. X-ray constraints come from non-observation of decay lines at E = m_s/2 in stacked clusters, M31, Galactic Center/Bulge and diffuse background with NuSTAR, Chandra and XMM-Newton. The 3.55 keV / 7.1 keV candidate has been extensively tested and largely excluded as DM decay. Production mechanism determines the relic density vs mixing relation and maps to the joint exclusion plane with Lyman-alpha free-streaming limits.

Key literature for this task:
- arXiv:1402.4119 — 7.1 keV sterile neutrino decay interpretation of the 3.55 keV line; defines X-ray line flux vs mass/mixing target.
- arXiv:1402.2301 — independent detection claim for the 3.55 keV line; motivates X-ray line search methodology.
- arXiv:1904.05710 — NuSTAR M31 / Galactic bulge X-ray line search with focused+unfocused FOV treatment.
- arXiv:1602.04816 — NuSTAR Galactic Center constraints closing the Dodelson-Widrow window.
- arXiv:1408.3503 — joint CMB/BBN N_eff and mass constraints vs short-baseline anomalies.
- arXiv:1103.4570 — comprehensive BBN+CMB+LSS constraints on sterile thermalization and Delta N_eff.

Additional papers referenced in this wave: arXiv:1705.01837 (Abazajian review), arXiv:2405.17861 (NuSTAR 11-yr stray-light), arXiv:2510.24560 (XRISM Resolve 3.75 Ms stacked clusters), arXiv:2507.18752 (Vogel Shi-Fuller with large L), astro-ph/0501562 (Viel et al. WDM/Lyman-alpha), astro-ph/0602028 (galaxy surface photometry, not directly relevant).

## Results

### BBN baseline and validity range
The sterile-neutrino server reports BBN baselines as Yp = 0.2449 ± 0.004 (Aver, Olive & Skillman JCAP 07 2021 029), D/H = 2.547 ± 0.025e-5 (Cooke, Pettini & Steidel ApJ 855 2018 102), Planck N_eff = 2.99 ± 0.17 (TT,TE,EE+lowE+lensing+BAO), with CMB-S4 forecast N_eff = 3.044 ± 0.03. The BBN fit validity range is N_eff 2.044–6.044, omega_b h2 0.019–0.0257, tau_n 866.4–890.4 s, 95% exclusion at Delta chi2 > 3.84 (1 dof), m_s < ~100 keV (relativistic at BBN), PRyMordial-calibrated <0.3%. This provenance was captured verbatim from the server description and has not been independently verified against primary observational papers; the brief’s alternative baselines Yp = 0.245 ± 0.003 and D/H = (2.53 ± 0.03)e-5 were not reconciled, and the impact of the Planck N_eff prior on the Delta N_eff < 0.5 vs 0.6 bound was not quantified.

### Prior-run artifacts and current-run inventory
Prior run 261021_110150 produced a DW scan CSV/NPZ (scan_DW_dc7743.csv/.npz), BBN vs N_eff plot (bbn_vs_neff.png), exclusion plane (exclusion_scan_DW_dc7743.png), six sterile_nu_grid CSVs (DW and SF mechanisms), and references.bib with five papers, plus six paper PDF/TXT pairs (1702.08430, 1705.01837, 2405.17861, 2507.18752, 2510.24560, astro-ph/0501562). Current run 261102_164917 contains three grid CSVs (sterile_nu_grid_DW_44fa64.csv, sterile_nu_grid_DW_5d6c37.csv, sterile_nu_grid_SF_d58c80.csv) and four figure directories (figures_1705.01837, figures_2405.17861, figures_astro-ph_0501562, figures_astro-ph_0602028). The out/ directory is empty (0 files); no updated joint report was written in this wave.

### X-ray decay-line emulator at contrasting masses
Two contrasting X-ray line predictions were computed with the server’s whole-halo, f_DM = 1, no FOV cut model (10 tabulated limits). This model assumption means the “not excluded” verdicts are not directly comparable to NuSTAR unfocused stray-light or SPI diffuse limits without primary-paper J-factor/profile and sin^2 2theta normalization.

- m_s = 40 keV, sin^2 2theta = 3e-14: E_gamma = 20 keV, Gamma = 4.18e-28 s^-1, tau = 2.39e27 s (7.58e19 yr), not excluded by built-in limits. Fluxes: Milky Way center (M = 1e12 Msun, d = 0.0083 Mpc) 1.42 ph/s/cm2; M31 (1.3e12 Msun, 0.78 Mpc) 0.000208 ph/s/cm2; Coma (1.2e15 Msun, 99.0 Mpc) 1.19e-05 ph/s/cm2; Perseus (6.6e14 Msun, 77.7 Mpc) 1.07e-05 ph/s/cm2.
- m_s = 10 keV, sin^2 2theta = 1e-12: E_gamma = 5 keV, Gamma = 1.36e-29 s^-1, tau = 7.35e28 s (2.33e21 yr), not excluded. Fluxes: Milky Way center 0.184 ph/s/cm2; M31 2.71e-05 ph/s/cm2; Coma 1.55e-06 ph/s/cm2; Perseus 1.4e-06 ph/s/cm2.

The analytic decay rate Gamma = 1.38e-29 s^-1 (m_s/1 keV)^5 sin^2 2theta matches the tool within 3% at these points. These two points are the only masses in the intended 5-row table (7.1/10/20/40/50 keV) with tool Gamma/tau in this wave; the 7.1 keV and 20 keV entries from prior waves were not rerun here, and the 50 keV SPI-dominated entry remains without primary-source provenance.

### BBN impact at high-mass, low-mixing (SPI-dominated) regime
A six-point DW grid at m_s = 40 and 50 keV with sin^2 2theta = 1e-12, 3e-14, 1e-14 was computed. All points are BBN-allowed (Delta chi2_BBN ~ 0, bbn_excluded_95 = 0) and not overclosing (Omega_s h2 < 0.12), confirming BBN is negligible at these low mixings where X-ray/SPI dominates. This result relies on the server’s BBN mapping and has not been independently verified with a full Boltzmann code.
